messages.content: What is the largest planet in the universe?

function.name: space_star_info

message.content:
There isn’t a single “largest planet in the universe” that we can point to with certainty—our knowledge is limited to the planets we’ve actually observed.  The largest planet that has been confirmed so far is the super‑Jupiter **HD 100546 b**, which orbits the young star HD 100546.  It has a mass of roughly 6–7 Jupiter masses (about 2 × 10²⁴ kg) and a radius of about 1.5–2 times that of Jupiter.  

Because we can only detect planets that happen to be in the right place at the right time, it’s entirely possible that larger planets exist elsewhere in the cosmos that we simply haven’t found yet.  In short, the “largest planet” is a moving target, and the current record holder is HD 100546 b.
